title: Perfect scalar models for dualizable complexes at geometric points
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] with scalar ring $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$, and $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field. Every dualizable object $N$ of the ordinary unbounded derived category $D((\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ admits a perfect $P\in D(R)$ and an isomorphism $N\cong L_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}(P)$, where $L$ is the scalar realization [def-zl-condensed-scalar-realization].

proof.text: the geometric-field profinite-site equivalence identifies the specified point inverse image with an exact symmetric monoidal equivalence on coefficient modules. Pass termwise to ordinary unbounded derived categories. The singleton profinite set is extremally disconnected. Contractible lisse evaluation there identifies dualizable complexes with perfect complexes over its coefficient section ring. That ring is R = Gamma(*, Lambda), by the terminal-section comparison, including multiplication and unit. Transport a bounded finite-projective representative along this ring isomorphism to obtain P. The scalar compatibility of evaluation identifies its realization with the original complex. This includes the zero ring and zero complex.
